title: The South Frederick Corridors Plan
summary: A district-scale redevelopment framework for transforming auto-oriented corridors into connected, walkable neighborhoods.
challenge: Create a realistic urban structure for incremental redevelopment across fragmented parcels and infrastructure constraints.
approach: Developed a street-and-block network, public-space hierarchy, development areas, and implementation logic that could guide parcel-by-parcel change.
outcome: A spatial and regulatory framework linking long-range vision to implementable development decisions.

title: South Frederick Monocacy Square
summary: A phased sequence showing how redevelopment projects, public investment, and the incremental completion of a connected street network can build out the South Frederick vision over time.

title: Form-Based Regulatory System
summary: A regulatory system translating an urban design vision into predictable standards, diagrams, processes, and implementation tools.
challenge: Turn design intent into a regulatory system that is precise enough to administer and simple enough to explain.
approach: Combined ordinance writing, process design, diagrams, dimensional standards, and implementation sequencing.
outcome: A coordinated system that connects policy, physical design, development review, and long-term implementation.

title: The Livable Frederick Master Plan
summary: A long-range policy framework integrating land use, mobility, housing, infrastructure, and community priorities.
challenge: Translate a broad set of community goals, technical inputs, and policy constraints into a coherent long-range framework.
approach: Structured the plan around clear policy choices, spatial frameworks, implementation actions, and visual explanations that connect policy to place.
outcome: A legible planning framework that supports decision-making, public communication, and future implementation.

title: Village Center Design Guidelines
summary: A visual companion to Frederick County's Village Center zoning standards that translates regulatory language into clear spatial principles.

title: Union Station Area Plan
summary: Urban design and implementation study for Worcester Union Station, linking intermodal transportation, circulation, public realm improvements, and surrounding redevelopment.

title: Virginia Beach Town Center
summary: A design study exploring how mixed uses can be assembled vertically within a connected urban block framework.

title: Hartford Busway Transit Oriented Development
summary: A corridor-scale transit-oriented development study for the New Britain–Hartford Busway.

title: MBTA Air Rights Development Study
summary: A design study exploring how mixed uses can be assembled vertically within a connected urban block framework.

title: Hybrid Church/Office Building
summary: A study of Manhattan churches as the analytical basis for a new church on a small site beside the former World Trade Center.

title: Route 101 Corridor Plan
location: Amherst, Bedford, Milford, and Wilton, New Hampshire
summary: A multidisciplinary corridor plan that connects transportation safety with access management, land use, environmental resources, visual character, landscape design, and long-term implementation.

title: Burlington Multi-modal Transit Center
summary: Conceptual design study for Burlington's Multi-Modal Transportation Center

title: Comprehensive Plan Land Use Data
summary: An interactive visualization for comparing land-use acreage across community growth areas.
challenge: Make a large set of land-use acreage data understandable across multiple growth areas.
approach: Combined an interactive map with selectable land-use categories and comparative bar-chart views.
outcome: A compact visual tool for exploring geographic and land-use patterns interactively.

title: County-to-County Worker Flow
summary: An interactive map for exploring residence-to-workplace commuter flows among counties in the region.
challenge: Show directional commuting relationships without reducing the data to a static table.
approach: Built an interactive origin-destination map with selectable residence and workplace counties.
outcome: A direct way to isolate and compare regional worker-flow relationships.
